questions.question_text: A square has diagonal 15√2 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: For square d=s√2, s=15; area=s²=225 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 7; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the ratio of the areas of the incircle and circumcircle of a square.
questions.explanation: R/r=√2 for a square, so πr²:πR²=1:2.
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 10; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A rhombus has area 315 cm² and perimeter 180 cm. Find its altitude.
questions.explanation: Side=180/4=45 cm; area=base×height, so height=315/45=7 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 11; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A rhombus has diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm. Find its area.
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 12; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A rhombus has side 13 cm and one diagonal 10 cm. Find the other diagonal.
questions.explanation: Diagonals bisect at right angles: half of other diagonal=√(13²−5²)=12; full diagonal=24 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 13; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A rhombus has perimeter 40 cm and one diagonal 16 cm. Find the other diagonal.
questions.explanation: Side=10; half first diagonal=8; other half=√(10²−8²)=6, so diagonal=12 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 14; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A square has area 200 cm². Its side is doubled. What is the new area?
questions.explanation: Area scales as side²; new area=4×200=800 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 16; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A square wire encloses 121 cm². It is reshaped into a circle. Using π=22/7, find the circle's area.
questions.explanation: Square side=11, perimeter/wire=44; circle radius=44/(2π)=7; area=π×49=154 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 17; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Using π=22/7, find the greatest circle area that fits inside a square of side 21 cm.
questions.explanation: Inscribed circle diameter=21, r=10.5; area=(22/7)×10.5²=346.5 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 18; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: An equilateral triangle is drawn on a square's diagonal. What is the ratio of the triangle area to the square area?
questions.explanation: Square diagonal=d; triangle area=√3d²/4; square area=d²/2; ratio=√3:2.
questions.source: Mensuration 1.pdf, PDF page 19; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the area of an isosceles triangle with sides 5 cm, 5 cm and base 8 cm.
questions.explanation: Altitude bisects base: h=√(5²−4²)=3; area=8×3/2=12 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 02.pdf, PDF page 11; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: An isosceles triangle has perimeter 40 cm and equal-side:base ratio 7:6. Find its area.
questions.source: Mensuration 02.pdf, PDF page 13; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm.

questions.question_text: A 5-12-13 right triangle has a median drawn to its hypotenuse. Find the median length.
questions.explanation: In a right triangle, median to hypotenuse equals half the hypotenuse: 13/2=6.5 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 02.pdf, PDF page 18; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: An isosceles triangle has base 10 cm and area 20 cm². Find the length of each equal side.
questions.source: Mensuration 02.pdf, PDF page 12; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A right triangle has inradius 3 cm and circumradius 12.5 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: For right triangle hypotenuse=2R=25; area=r×semiperimeter. Legs satisfy a+b=25+2r=31 and a²+b²=625; ab=168; area=ab/2=84 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 02.pdf, PDF page 19; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.source: Mensuration 3.pdf, PDF page 9; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A parallelogram has adjacent sides 60 cm and 40 cm and a diagonal 80 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: Triangle sides 60,40,80 have s=90; Heron area=√(90×30×50×10)=300√15 cm²; the parallelogram is twice that, so area=600√15 cm².
questions.source: Mensuration 3.pdf, PDF page 12; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A parallelogram has adjacent sides 12 cm and 14 cm; one diagonal is 16 cm. Find the other diagonal.
questions.explanation: Parallelogram law: d₁²+d₂²=2(12²+14²)=680; d₂²=424; d₂=2√106 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 3.pdf, PDF page 13; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A parallelogram's sides are in ratio 3:2, its area is 243 cm², and included angle is 30°. Find its perimeter.
questions.explanation: Let sides 3x,2x. Area=3x·2x·sin30=3x²=243, x=9; perimeter=2(27+18)=90 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 3.pdf, PDF page 15; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A trapezium has area 384 cm², parallel-side ratio 3:5, and height 12 cm. Find the shorter parallel side.
questions.explanation: 384=12(a+b)/2 gives a+b=64; ratio parts total 8, one part=8; shorter=3×8=24 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 3.pdf, PDF page 19; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A trapezium has area 180 cm² and height 9 cm. One parallel side is 6 cm longer than the other. Find the shorter side.
questions.explanation: Sum of parallel sides=2A/h=40; solve x+(x+6)=40, x=17 cm.
questions.source: Mensuration 3.pdf, PDF page 20; slide deck labels section as PYQ but individual exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the triangle side is 12 cm, find the square area.
